# These are the complete eight laws of the observed polymorphic sum encoding.
# Projection laws imply constructor injectivity; the distinct index equations
# imply disjointness; the last law gives exhaustiveness. The two polymorphic
# match equations then agree with either constructor for every result sort.
# This is a datatype interpretation, never an imported desired source theorem.
CELL_LAWS = (
    '(par (a) (forall ((z a) (z1 a) (u Int)) (= (match_cell (Integer u) z z1) z)))',
    '(par (a) (forall ((z a) (z1 a) (u Int) (u1 Int)) (= (match_cell (Pointer u u1) z z1) z1)))',
    '(forall ((u Int)) (= (index_cell (Integer u)) 0))',
    '(forall ((u Int) (u1 Int)) (= (index_cell (Pointer u u1)) 1))',
    '(forall ((u Int)) (= (Integer_proj_1 (Integer u)) u))',
    '(forall ((u Int) (u1 Int)) (= (Pointer_proj_1 (Pointer u u1)) u))',
    '(forall ((u Int) (u1 Int)) (= (Pointer_proj_2 (Pointer u u1)) u1))',
    '(forall ((u cell)) (or (= u (Integer (Integer_proj_1 u))) '
    '(= u (Pointer (Pointer_proj_1 u) (Pointer_proj_2 u)))))',
)

CELL_DECLARATIONS = (
    '(declare-sort cell 0)',
    '(declare-fun Integer (Int) cell)',
    '(declare-fun Pointer (Int Int) cell)',
    '(declare-fun match_cell (par (a) (cell a a) a))',

    '(declare-fun Pointer_proj_1 (cell) Int)',
    '(declare-fun Pointer_proj_2 (cell) Int)',

def need(value, label):
    if not value:
        raise ValueError(label)


def replace_symbols(tree, aliases):
    """Closed vocabulary renaming; full typed parameter rows remain compared."""
    if isinstance(tree, str):
        return aliases.get(tree, tree)
    return [replace_symbols(item, aliases) for item in tree]


def normalize_source_primitives(tree):
    """Only two source aliases and complete Integer/Pointer projection matches.

    Call after the closed per-task cell declaration/law check. Match binders
    disappear only when the entire branch is its own selected Int field or
    literal zero. No arbitrary selector, constructor or branch is eliminated.
    """
    if isinstance(tree, str):
        return tree
    need(isinstance(tree, list) and tree, 'nonempty complete mathematical term')
    if tree[0] == 'H_fresh_id':
        need(len(tree) == 2, 'exact source fresh_id application')
        return ['next', normalize_source_primitives(tree[1])]
    if tree[0] == 'H_end_automatic':
        need(len(tree) == 3, 'exact source end_automatic application')
        return ['H_release', *(normalize_source_primitives(x) for x in tree[1:])]
    if tree[0] == 'match_cell':
        need(len(tree) == 4, 'complete typed cell match application')
        value, integer, pointer = tree[1:]
        if integer == ['Integer_proj_1', value] and pointer == '0':
            return ['_source9_integer_or_zero', normalize_source_primitives(value)]
        if integer == '0' and pointer == ['Pointer_proj_1', value]:
            return ['_source9_pointer_target_or_zero', normalize_source_primitives(value)]
        raise ValueError('unrecognized complete cell projection match')
    if tree[0] == 'match':
        need(len(tree) == 3 and isinstance(tree[2], list) and len(tree[2]) == 2,
             'complete two-constructor cell source match')
        cases = {}
        for case in tree[2]:
            need(isinstance(case, list) and len(case) == 2 and isinstance(case[0], list),
                 'closed cell constructor branch')
            pattern, body = case
            name = pattern[0]
            need(name in {'Integer', 'Pointer'} and name not in cases
                 and len(pattern) == (2 if name == 'Integer' else 3)
                 and all(isinstance(x, str) for x in pattern[1:])
                 and len(set(pattern[1:])) == len(pattern)-1, 'complete source sum constructor fields')
            cases[name] = (pattern[1:], body)
        need(set(cases) == {'Integer', 'Pointer'}, 'both source constructors required')
        integer, pointer = cases['Integer'], cases['Pointer']
        if integer[1] == integer[0][0] and pointer[1] == '0':
            return ['_source9_integer_or_zero', normalize_source_primitives(tree[1])]
        if integer[1] == '0' and pointer[1] == pointer[0][0]:
            return ['_source9_pointer_target_or_zero', normalize_source_primitives(tree[1])]
        raise ValueError('source match does not have the complete selected projection branches')
    return [normalize_source_primitives(item) if isinstance(item, list) and item else item
            for item in tree]


def task_context(commands, parse, canonical):
    """Check every declaration, complete record products and the cell encoding.

    `parse` and `canonical` are the separately reviewed syntax/alpha helpers.
    No definition body or source goal is accepted by this context alone. The
    caller must reconcile every complete definition/support/goal afterward.
    """
    pending = [commands]
    while pending:
        item = pending.pop()
        if isinstance(item, str):
            need(not item.startswith('_source9_'), 'private interpretation vocabulary cannot occur in actual input')
        else:
            need(isinstance(item, list), 'complete mathematical syntax node')
            pending.extend(item)
    declarations = [row for row in commands if row[0].startswith('declare-')]
    sums = [row for row in declarations if row[0] == 'declare-datatypes'
            and row[1] == [['cell', '0']]]
    abstract = [row for row in declarations if row == ['declare-sort', 'cell', '0']]
    need(len(sums)+len(abstract) == 1, 'exactly one selected complete cell encoding')
    aliases, consumed, support = {}, [], []
    for sort, fields, name in (
        ('heap', HEAP_FIELDS, 'mk_heap'),
        ('state', (('active', '(Array Int Bool)'), ('backing', '(Array Int Int)')), 'mk_state'),
    ):
        rows = [row for row in declarations if row[0] == 'declare-datatypes'
                and row[1] == [[sort, '0']]]
        need(len(rows) == 1 and len(rows[0]) == 3 and len(rows[0][2]) == 1
             and len(rows[0][2][0]) == 1, 'complete single-constructor source record')
        constructor = rows[0][2][0][0]
        expected = [[field, parse(typ)] for field, typ in fields]
        need(isinstance(constructor[0], str) and constructor[1:] == expected,
             'complete ordered record field names and sorts')
        aliases[constructor[0]] = name
        consumed.append(rows[0])
    if sums:
        expected = parse('(declare-datatypes ((cell 0)) '
            '(((Integer (Integer_proj Int)) (Pointer (Pointer_proj Int) (Pointer_proj1 Int)))))')
        need(sums[0] == expected, 'complete native Integer/Pointer datatype fields')
        consumed.append(sums[0])
        mode = 'native_algebraic_sum'
    else:
        mode = 'closed_axiomatized_polymorphic_sum'
        for source in CELL_DECLARATIONS:
            expected = parse(source)
            need(declarations.count(expected) == 1, 'complete exact typed cell declaration')
            consumed.append(expected)
        assertions = [row for row in commands if row[0] == 'assert'][:-1]
        for source in CELL_LAWS:
            target = canonical(parse(source))
            matches = [row for row in assertions if canonical(row[1]) == target]
            need(len(matches) == 1, 'complete unique source sum encoding law')
            support.append(matches[0])
    for name in ('div1', 'mod1'):
        expected = parse('(declare-fun '+name+' (Int Int) Int)')
        need(declarations.count(expected) == 1, 'complete integer division signature')
        consumed.append(expected)
    constants = {}
    fc = parse('(declare-fun fc () (Array Int Bool))')
    if fc in declarations:
        need(declarations.count(fc) == 1, 'unique complete constant-map declaration')
        target = canonical(parse('(forall ((us Int)) (= (select fc us) false))'))
        assertions = [row for row in commands if row[0] == 'assert'][:-1]
        matches = [row for row in assertions if canonical(row[1]) == target]
        need(len(matches) == 1, 'complete typed false-map defining equation')
        consumed.append(fc); support.append(matches[0])
        constants['fc'] = parse('((as const (Array Int Bool)) false)')
    need(len(consumed) == len(declarations) and all(row in consumed for row in declarations),
         'no extra sort, function, constant or record declaration')
    # Candidates are named only after the entire parameter/result signature
    # matches. Complete bodies remain mandatory in the caller's next stage.
    for row in commands:
        if row[0] != 'define-fun':
            continue
        need(len(row) == 5 and isinstance(row[2], list), 'complete typed function definition')
        role = 'H_'+row[1]
        if role in HEAP_DEFINITIONS:
            params, result, _ = HEAP_DEFINITIONS[role]
            need([x[1] for x in row[2]] == [x[1] for x in parse('('+params+')')]
                 and row[3] == parse(result), 'complete Heap parameter/result signature')
            aliases[row[1]] = role
    return {'mode': mode, 'aliases': aliases, 'constants': constants,
            'declarations': consumed, 'sum_and_map_support': support,
            'definition_goal_or_scientific_acceptance': False}


def positional_body(parameters, body):
    """Alpha-rename function arguments by position, never by permutation.

    Function arguments are ordered even when their sorts coincide. Bound local
    variables are protected from substitution, including simultaneous let and
    the two constructor patterns. Private names cannot occur in actual tasks.
    """
    need(all(isinstance(row, list) and len(row) == 2 and isinstance(row[0], str)
             for row in parameters), 'closed typed function parameter rows')
    need(len({row[0] for row in parameters}) == len(parameters), 'unique ordered function parameters')
    environment = {row[0]: '_source9_parameter_'+str(index)
                   for index, row in enumerate(parameters)}
    def rename(tree, env):
        if isinstance(tree, str):
            return env.get(tree, tree)
        need(isinstance(tree, list) and tree, 'nonempty complete positional term')
        if tree[0] in ('forall', 'exists'):
            need(len(tree) == 3 and all(isinstance(row, list) and len(row) == 2 for row in tree[1]),
                 'complete inner binder in positional body')
            local = {key: value for key, value in env.items() if key not in {row[0] for row in tree[1]}}
            return [tree[0], tree[1], rename(tree[2], local)]
        if tree[0] == 'let':
            need(len(tree) == 3 and all(isinstance(row, list) and len(row) == 2 for row in tree[1]),
                 'complete simultaneous let in positional body')
            local = {key: value for key, value in env.items() if key not in {row[0] for row in tree[1]}}
            return ['let', [[row[0], rename(row[1], env)] for row in tree[1]], rename(tree[2], local)]
        if tree[0] == 'match':
            need(len(tree) == 3, 'complete sum match in positional body')
            cases = []
            for pattern, value in tree[2]:
                need(isinstance(pattern, list) and pattern, 'complete constructor pattern')
                local = {key: mapped for key, mapped in env.items() if key not in set(pattern[1:])}
                cases.append([pattern, rename(value, local)])
            return ['match', rename(tree[1], env), cases]
        return [rename(item, env) if isinstance(item, list) and item else
                env.get(item, item) if isinstance(item, str) else item for item in tree]
    return rename(body, environment)


def reconcile_heap_definitions(commands, context, parse, canonical):
    """Compare every observed Heap definition against its complete source body.

    The function's full parameter sorts and result sort are checked by
    task_context. Fixed aliases identify the complete source vocabulary, and
    the sum/false-map rules apply only after their complete context checks.
    Missing source-inlined fresh_id/end_automatic definitions are not invented.
    Other functions/support/goals remain the outer reader's separate duties.
    """
    aliases = {**context['aliases'], **context['constants']}
    matched = []
    for row in commands:
        if row[0] != 'define-fun':
            continue
        role = context['aliases'].get(row[1], '')
        if not role.startswith('H_'):
            continue
        parameters, result, body = HEAP_DEFINITIONS[role]
        expected = positional_body(parse('('+parameters+')'), parse(body))
        actual = positional_body(row[2], row[4])
        def normal(term):
            return canonical(normalize_source_primitives(replace_symbols(term, aliases)))
        need(row[3] == parse(result) and normal(actual) == normal(expected),
             'complete source Heap definition mismatch: '+role)
        matched.append({'name': row[1], 'role': role, 'complete_typed_body_equal': True})
    return matched

def source_goal_text(ident):

SCIENTIFIC_ACCEPTANCE = False
SOURCE_HEAP_TYPED_CALLER_ACCEPTANCE = False


def need(value, label):
    if not value:
        raise ValueError(label)


def digest(tree):
    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(tree, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'),
                                     allow_nan=False).encode()).hexdigest()


def rename_globals(tree, aliases, bound=frozenset()):
    """Rename only free symbols; preserve all quantifier/let/match scopes.

    The aliases are candidate typed source roles, whose complete definition
    bodies must subsequently match. They never establish a source fact alone.
    """
    if isinstance(tree, str):
        return tree if tree in bound else aliases.get(tree, tree)
    need(isinstance(tree, list) and tree, 'complete nonempty scoped term')
    if tree[0] in ('forall', 'exists'):
        need(len(tree) == 3 and all(isinstance(row, list) and len(row) == 2
                                   for row in tree[1]), 'complete quantified bindings')
        local = bound | {row[0] for row in tree[1]}
        return [tree[0], tree[1], rename_globals(tree[2], aliases, local)]
    if tree[0] == 'let':
        need(len(tree) == 3 and all(isinstance(row, list) and len(row) == 2
                                   for row in tree[1]), 'complete simultaneous let')
        bindings = [[row[0], rename_globals(row[1], aliases, bound)] for row in tree[1]]
        return ['let', bindings, rename_globals(tree[2], aliases,
                                               bound | {row[0] for row in tree[1]})]
    if tree[0] == 'match':
        need(len(tree) == 3, 'complete sum match')
        cases = []
        for pattern, body in tree[2]:
            need(isinstance(pattern, list) and pattern, 'complete constructor pattern')
            cases.append([[aliases.get(pattern[0], pattern[0]), *pattern[1:]],
                          rename_globals(body, aliases, bound | set(pattern[1:]))])
        return ['match', rename_globals(tree[1], aliases, bound), cases]
    return [rename_globals(item, aliases, bound) for item in tree]


def inline_source_aliases(tree):
    """The driver's two absent scalar accessors are exact source abbreviations."""
    if isinstance(tree, str):
        return tree
    need(isinstance(tree, list) and tree, 'complete source alias term')
    if tree[0] in ('E_size', 'E_capacity'):
        need(len(tree) == 3, 'complete typed header scalar accessor')
        return ['H_load_int', inline_source_aliases(tree[1]),
                inline_source_aliases(tree[2]), '8' if tree[0] == 'E_size' else '16']
    return [inline_source_aliases(item) if isinstance(item, list) and item else item
            for item in tree]


def _sort_signature(parameters, result):
    need(isinstance(parameters, list) and all(isinstance(row, list) and len(row) == 2
                                             and isinstance(row[0], str) for row in parameters),
         'complete ordered typed parameters')
    need(len({row[0] for row in parameters}) == len(parameters), 'unique function parameter names')
    return [row[1] for row in parameters], result


def candidate_roles(commands, context, parse):
    """Disambiguate overloads by entire ordered typed signatures, then compare bodies.

    Numeric suffixes are merely driver spelling candidates. A missing or
    altered complete body remains a hard refusal in reconcile_task.
    """
    aliases = dict(context['aliases'])
    rows = [row for row in commands if row[0] == 'define-fun']
    need(len({row[1] for row in rows}) == len(rows), 'unique actual task function definitions')
    signatures = {role: _sort_signature(parse('('+parameters+')'), parse(result))
                  for role, (parameters, result, _) in OWNERS_EFFECTS_DEFINITIONS.items()}
    for row in rows:
        need(len(row) == 5, 'complete actual definition shape')
        if row[1] in aliases:
            continue
        actual_signature = _sort_signature(row[2], row[3])
        matches = []
        for role, signature in signatures.items():
            base = role[2:]
            spelling = row[1]
            suffix = spelling[len(base):] if spelling.startswith(base) else None
            if suffix is not None and (suffix == '' or suffix.isdecimal() and not suffix.startswith('0')) \
                    and signature == actual_signature:
                matches.append(role)
        need(len(matches) <= 1, 'unique fully typed source role candidate')
        if matches:
            aliases[row[1]] = matches[0]
    return aliases


# A complete explicit alpha-renaming certificate. The correspondence is checked
# against every original binder name, sort and position on both sides. Reordering
# a closed universal block is sound; no binder crosses an implication/exists.
GOAL_BINDER_MAP = {
    'move': {'h': 'heap1', 'owners': 'state1', 'ready': 't', 'd': 'i2',
             's': 'i4', 'b': 'i', 'n': 'i3', 'c': 'i1'},
    'swap': {'h': 'heap1', 'owners': 'state1', 'ready': 't', 'l': 'i5', 'r': 'i8',
             'a': 'i', 'bl': 'i1', 'nl': 'i6', 'cl': 'i3', 'br': 'i2',
             'nr': 'i7', 'cr': 'i4'},
}


def reconcile_task(commands, ident, context, parse, canonical, normalize_primitives):
    """Compare complete typed Owners/Effects definitions and one full source goal.

    This does not consume unrelated definitions/support, adopt native results,
    prove source effects, or enable any source/Heap/Typed/caller route. The outer
    cold join must account for every command and every imported assertion.
    """
    need(ident in CONCLUSIONS, 'one of the nine exact original source duties')
    pending = [commands]
    while pending:
        item = pending.pop()
        if isinstance(item, str):
            need(not item.startswith(('$source9_', '_source9_', 'H_', 'O_', 'E_'))
                 and item not in {'mk_heap', 'mk_state'}, 'private source interpretation vocabulary')
        else:
            need(isinstance(item, list), 'complete retained mathematical syntax')
            pending.extend(item)
    aliases = candidate_roles(commands, context, parse)
    aliases.update(context['constants'])

    def normalized(body, parameters, prefix):
        names = [row[0] for row in parameters]
        need(len(set(names)) == len(names), 'unique complete alpha parameters')
        env = {name: '$source9_'+prefix+str(index) for index, name in enumerate(names)}
        renamed = rename_globals(body, aliases, frozenset(names))
        expanded = normalize_primitives(inline_source_aliases(renamed))
        return canonical(expanded, env=env)

    definitions, unhandled = [], []
    for row in commands:
        if row[0] != 'define-fun':
            continue
        role = aliases.get(row[1])
        if role not in OWNERS_EFFECTS_DEFINITIONS:
            unhandled.append(row)
            continue
        parameters, result, body = OWNERS_EFFECTS_DEFINITIONS[role]
        source_parameters = parse('('+parameters+')')
        need(_sort_signature(row[2], row[3]) == _sort_signature(source_parameters, parse(result)),
             'complete ordered source signature: '+role)
        actual = normalized(row[4], row[2], 'argument')
        expected = normalized(parse(body), source_parameters, 'argument')
        need(actual == expected, 'complete position-preserving source definition mismatch: '+role)
        definitions.append({'actual_name': row[1], 'role': role,
                            'command_sha256': digest(row),
                            'actual_ordered_parameters': row[2],
                            'source_ordered_parameters': source_parameters,
                            'result_sort': row[3],
                            'complete_normalized_body_sha256': digest(actual),
                            'complete_ordered_signature_and_body_equal': True})

    assertions = [row for row in commands if row[0] == 'assert']
    need(assertions and all(len(row) == 2 for row in assertions), 'complete assertion census')
    actual = assertions[-1][1]
    expected = parse(source_goal_text(ident))
    for term in (actual, expected):
        need(isinstance(term, list) and len(term) == 2 and term[0] == 'not'
             and isinstance(term[1], list) and len(term[1]) == 3 and term[1][0] == 'forall',
             'complete negated closed universal source goal')
        _sort_signature(term[1][1], 'Bool')
    source_parameters, actual_parameters = expected[1][1], actual[1][1]
    correspondence = GOAL_BINDER_MAP[ident.split('.')[0]]
    source_sorts = dict(source_parameters)
    actual_sorts = dict(actual_parameters)
    need(set(correspondence) == set(source_sorts)
         and set(correspondence.values()) == set(actual_sorts)
         and len(correspondence.values()) == len(set(correspondence.values()))
         and all(source_sorts[name] == actual_sorts[other]
                 for name, other in correspondence.items()),
         'total bijective complete typed universal goal correspondence')
    actual_in_source_order = [[correspondence[name], typ] for name, typ in source_parameters]
    actual_body = normalized(actual[1][2], actual_in_source_order, 'goal')
    source_body = normalized(expected[1][2], source_parameters, 'goal')
    need(actual_body == source_body, 'entire original antecedent and conclusion mismatch: '+ident)

    # Every direct/transitive source role referenced by the full source goal
    # must be observed with its complete body or be an exact declared alias.
    observed = {row['role'] for row in definitions} | set(context['aliases'].values())
    primitive = {'E_size', 'E_capacity', 'H_fresh_id', 'H_end_automatic'}
    required, queue = set(), [expected]
    while queue:
        item = queue.pop()
        if isinstance(item, str):
            if item in OWNERS_EFFECTS_DEFINITIONS and item not in required:
                required.add(item)
                queue.append(parse(OWNERS_EFFECTS_DEFINITIONS[item][2]))
        else:
            queue.extend(item)
    need(required <= observed | primitive, 'complete source role dependency closure')
    return {'id': ident, 'definitions': definitions, 'own_definition_count': len(definitions),
            'all_observed_own_definitions_equivalent': True, 'source_goal_equivalent': True,
            'actual_complete_goal_command_sha256': digest(assertions[-1]),
            'source_complete_goal_sha256': digest(expected),
            'complete_normalized_goal_body_sha256': digest(actual_body),
            'actual_complete_goal_binders': actual_parameters,
            'source_complete_goal_binders': source_parameters,
            'goal_binder_correspondence': correspondence,
            'complete_goal_source_roles': sorted(required),
            'unhandled_complete_definitions': unhandled,
            'support_assertions_not_consumed_here': assertions[:-1],
            'complete_support_or_scientific_acceptance': False,
            'source_Heap_Typed_caller_admission': False}

theory Qed

  use bool.Bool
  use int.Int
  use real.RealInfix
  use real.FromInt
  use int.ComputerDivision as CD

  (** The definitions are in comment because its not useful for coq
      (no if-then-else on formula) and not tested on automatic provers *)

  function eqb (x y : 'a) : bool = if x = y then True else False
  function neqb (x y : 'a) : bool = if x <> y then True else False

  function zlt  (x y : int) : bool = if x < y  then True else False
  function zleq (x y : int) : bool = if x <= y then True else False

  function rlt  (x y : real) : bool = if x <. y  then True else False
  function rleq (x y : real) : bool = if x <=. y then True else False

  function real_of_int (x:int) : real = FromInt.from_int x
  meta "inline:no" function real_of_int

  lemma c_euclidian : forall n d:int [(CD.div n d),(CD.mod n d)].
    d <> 0 -> n = CD.div n d * d + CD.mod n d

  lemma cmod_remainder : forall n d:int [CD.mod n d].
    ((n >= 0) -> (d > 0) ->  0 <= CD.mod n d <  d) /\
    ((n <= 0) -> (d > 0) -> -d <  CD.mod n d <= 0) /\
    ((n >= 0) -> (d < 0) ->  0 <= CD.mod n d < -d) /\
    ((n <= 0) -> (d < 0) ->  d <  CD.mod n d <= 0)

  lemma cdiv_neutral : forall a:int [CD.div a 1]. CD.div a 1 = a
  lemma cdiv_inv : forall a:int [CD.div a a]. a<>0 -> CD.div a a = 1

  lemma cdiv_closed_remainder :
    forall a,b,n:int.
    0 <= a -> 0 <= b -> 0 <= b-a < n ->
    CD.mod a n = CD.mod b n -> a = b
  by b - a = n * (CD.div (b - a) n) + CD.mod (b - a) n
  so (CD.div b n) - (CD.div a n) = CD.div (b - a) n
end

(** {1 Theory of integers}

This file provides the basic theory of integers, and several additional
theories for classical functions.

*)

(** {2 Integers and the basic operators} *)

module Int

  let constant zero : int = 0
  let constant one  : int = 1

  val (=) (x y : int) : bool ensures { result <-> x = y }

  val function  (-_) int : int
  val function  (+)  int int : int
  val function  (*)  int int : int
  val predicate (<)  int int : bool

  let function  (-)  (x y : int) = x + -y
  let predicate (>)  (x y : int) = y < x
  let predicate (<=) (x y : int) = x < y || x = y
  let predicate (>=) (x y : int) = y <= x

  clone export algebra.OrderedUnitaryCommutativeRing with
    type t = int, constant zero = zero, constant one = one,
    function (-_) = (-_), function (+) = (+),
    function (*) = (*), predicate (<=) = (<=)

  meta "remove_unused:keep" function (+)
  meta "remove_unused:keep" function (-)
(* do not necessarily keep, to allow for linear arithmetic only
  meta "remove_unused:keep" function (*)
*)
  meta "remove_unused:keep" function (-_)
  meta "remove_unused:keep" predicate (<)
  meta "remove_unused:keep" predicate (<=)
  meta "remove_unused:keep" predicate (>)
  meta "remove_unused:keep" predicate (>=)

end

(** {2 Absolute Value} *)

module Abs

  use Int

  let function abs (x:int) : int = if x >= 0 then x else -x

  lemma Abs_le: forall x y:int. abs x <= y <-> -y <= x <= y
  meta "remove_unused:dependency" lemma Abs_le, function abs

  lemma Abs_pos: forall x:int. abs x >= 0
  meta "remove_unused:dependency" lemma Abs_pos, function abs

(***
  lemma Abs_zero: forall x:int. abs x = 0 -> x = 0
*)

end

(** {2 Minimum and Maximum} *)

module MinMax

  use Int

(** {2 Euclidean Division}

Division and modulo operators with the convention
that modulo is always non-negative.

It implies that division rounds down when divisor is positive, and
rounds up when divisor is negative.

*)

module EuclideanDivision

  use Int
  use Abs

  function div (x y: int) : int
  function mod (x y: int) : int

  axiom Div_mod:
    forall x y:int. y <> 0 -> x = y * div x y + mod x y
  meta "remove_unused:dependency" axiom Div_mod, function div
  meta "remove_unused:dependency" axiom Div_mod, function mod

  axiom Mod_bound:
    forall x y:int. y <> 0 -> 0 <= mod x y < abs y
  meta "remove_unused:dependency" axiom Mod_bound, function mod

  lemma Div_unique:
    forall x y q:int. y > 0 -> q * y <= x < q * y + y -> div x y = q
  meta "remove_unused:dependency" lemma Div_unique, function div

  lemma Div_bound:
    forall x y:int. x >= 0 /\ y > 0 -> 0 <= div x y <= x
  meta "remove_unused:dependency" lemma Div_bound, function div

  lemma Mod_1: forall x:int. mod x 1 = 0
  meta "remove_unused:dependency" lemma Mod_1, function mod

  lemma Div_1: forall x:int. div x 1 = x
  meta "remove_unused:dependency" lemma Div_1, function div

  lemma Div_inf: forall x y:int. 0 <= x < y -> div x y = 0
  meta "remove_unused:dependency" lemma Div_inf, function div

  lemma Div_inf_neg: forall x y:int. 0 < x <= y -> div (-x) y = -1
  meta "remove_unused:dependency" lemma Div_inf_neg, function div

  lemma Mod_0: forall y:int. y <> 0 -> mod 0 y = 0
  meta "remove_unused:dependency" lemma Mod_0, function mod

  lemma Div_1_left: forall y:int. y > 1 -> div 1 y = 0
  meta "remove_unused:dependency" lemma Div_1_left, function div

  lemma Div_minus1_left: forall y:int. y > 1 -> div (-1) y = -1
  meta "remove_unused:dependency" lemma Div_minus1_left, function div

  lemma Mod_1_left: forall y:int. y > 1 -> mod 1 y = 1
  meta "remove_unused:dependency" lemma Mod_1_left, function mod

  lemma Mod_minus1_left: forall y:int. y > 1 -> mod (-1) y = y - 1
  meta "remove_unused:dependency" lemma Mod_minus1_left, function mod

  lemma Div_mult: forall x y z:int [div (x * y + z) x].
          x > 0 ->
          div (x * y + z) x = y + div z x
  meta "remove_unused:dependency" lemma Div_mult, function div

  lemma Mod_mult: forall x y z:int [mod (x * y + z) x].
          x > 0 ->
          mod (x * y + z) x = mod z x
  meta "remove_unused:dependency" lemma Mod_mult, function mod

  val div (x y:int) : int
    requires { y <> 0 }
    ensures { result = div x y }

  val mod (x y:int) : int
    requires { y <> 0 }
    ensures { result = mod x y }


end

(** {2 Number of integers satisfying a given predicate} *)

module NumOf

  use Int

  (** number of `n` such that `a <= n < b` and `p n` *)
  let rec function numof (p: int -> bool) (a b: int) : int
    variant { b - a }
  = if b <= a then 0 else
    if p (b - 1) then 1 + numof p a (b - 1)
                 else     numof p a (b - 1)

  lemma Numof_bounds :
    forall p : int -> bool, a b : int. a < b -> 0 <= numof p a b <= b - a
    (* direct when a>=b, by induction on b when a <= b *)

  lemma Numof_append :
    forall p : int -> bool, a b c : int.
    a <= b <= c -> numof p a c = numof p a b + numof p b c
    (* by induction on c *)

  lemma Numof_left_no_add :
    forall p : int -> bool, a b : int.
    a < b -> not p a -> numof p a b = numof p (a+1) b
    (* by Numof_append *)
  lemma Numof_left_add :
    forall p : int -> bool, a b : int.
    a < b -> p a -> numof p a b = 1 + numof p (a+1) b
    (* by Numof_append *)

  lemma Empty :
    forall p : int -> bool, a b : int.
    (forall n : int. a <= n < b -> not p n) -> numof p a b = 0
    (* by induction on b *)

  lemma Full :
    forall p : int -> bool, a b : int. a <= b ->
    (forall n : int. a <= n < b -> p n) -> numof p a b = b - a
    (* by induction on b *)

  lemma numof_increasing:
    forall p : int -> bool, i j k : int.
    i <= j <= k -> numof p i j <= numof p i k
    (* by Numof_append and Numof_non_negative *)

  lemma numof_strictly_increasing:
    forall p: int -> bool, i j k l: int.
    i <= j <= k < l -> p k -> numof p i j < numof p i l
    (* by Numof_append and numof_increasing *)

  lemma numof_change_any:
    forall p1 p2: int -> bool, a b: int.
    (forall j: int. a <= j < b -> p1 j -> p2 j) ->
    numof p2 a b >= numof p1 a b

  lemma numof_change_some:
    forall p1 p2: int -> bool, a b i: int. a <= i < b ->
    (forall j: int. a <= j < b -> p1 j -> p2 j) ->
    not (p1 i) -> p2 i ->
    numof p2 a b > numof p1 a b

  lemma numof_change_equiv:
    forall p1 p2: int -> bool, a b: int.
    (forall j: int. a <= j < b -> p1 j <-> p2 j) ->
    numof p2 a b = numof p1 a b

end

(** {2 Sum} *)

module Sum

  use Int

  (** sum of `f n` for `a <= n < b` *)
  let rec function sum (f: int -> int) (a b: int) : int
    variant { b - a }
  = if b <= a then 0 else sum f a (b - 1) + f (b - 1)

  lemma sum_left:
    forall f: int -> int, a b: int.
    a < b -> sum f a b = f a + sum f (a + 1) b

  lemma sum_ext:
    forall f g: int -> int, a b: int.
    (forall i. a <= i < b -> f i = g i) ->
    sum f a b = sum g a b

  lemma sum_le:
    forall f g: int -> int, a b: int.
    (forall i. a <= i < b -> f i <= g i) ->
    sum f a b <= sum g a b

  lemma sum_zero:
    forall f: int -> int, a b: int.
    (forall i. a <= i < b -> f i = 0) ->
    sum f a b = 0

  lemma sum_nonneg:
    forall f: int -> int, a b: int.
    (forall i. a <= i < b -> 0 <= f i) ->
    0 <= sum f a b

  lemma sum_decomp:
    forall f: int -> int, a b c: int. a <= b <= c ->
    sum f a c = sum f a b + sum f b c

  let rec lemma shift_left (f g: int -> int) (a b c d: int)
    requires { b - a = d - c }
    requires { forall i. a <= i < b -> f i  = g (c + i - a) }
    variant  { b - a }
    ensures  { sum f a b = sum g c d }
  = if a < b then shift_left f g (a+1) b (c+1) d

end

(** A similar theory, but with a polymorphic parameter passed
    to function `f` and to function `sum`. *)
module SumParam

  use Int

  (** sum of `f x n` for `a <= n < b` *)
  let rec function sum (f: 'a -> int -> int) (x: 'a) (a b: int) : int
    variant { b - a }
  = if b <= a then 0 else sum f x a (b - 1) + f x (b - 1)

  lemma sum_left:
    forall f: 'a -> int -> int, x: 'a, a b: int.
    a < b -> sum f x a b = f x a + sum f x (a + 1) b

  lemma sum_ext:
    forall f: 'a -> int -> int, x: 'a, g: 'b -> int -> int, y: 'b, a b: int.
    (forall i. a <= i < b -> f x i = g y i) ->
    sum f x a b = sum g y a b

  lemma sum_le:
    forall f: 'a -> int -> int, x: 'a, g: 'b -> int -> int, y: 'b, a b: int.
    (forall i. a <= i < b -> f x i <= g y i) ->
    sum f x a b <= sum g y a b

  lemma sum_zero:
    forall f: 'a -> int -> int, x: 'a, a b: int.
    (forall i. a <= i < b -> f x i = 0) ->
    sum f x a b = 0

  lemma sum_nonneg:
    forall f: 'a -> int -> int, x: 'a, a b: int.
    (forall i. a <= i < b -> 0 <= f x i) ->
    0 <= sum f x a b

  lemma sum_decomp:
    forall f: 'a -> int -> int, x: 'a, a b c: int. a <= b <= c ->
    sum f x a c = sum f x a b + sum f x b c

  let rec lemma shift_left
    (f: 'a -> int -> int) (x: 'a)
    (g: 'b -> int -> int) (y: 'b) (a b c d: int)
    requires { b - a = d - c }
    requires { forall i. a <= i < b -> f x i  = g y (c + i - a) }
    variant  { b - a }
    ensures  { sum f x a b = sum g y c d }
  = if a < b then shift_left f x g y (a+1) b (c+1) d

  let rec lemma sum_middle_change (f:'a -> int -> int) (c1 c2:'a) (i j l: int)
    requires { i <= l < j }
    ensures  { (forall k : int. i <= k < j -> k <> l -> f c1 k = f c2 k) ->
               sum f c1 i j - f c1 l = sum f c2 i j - f c2 l }
    variant  { j - l }
  = if l = (j-1) then () else sum_middle_change f c1 c2 i (j-1) l

end

(** {2 Factorial function} *)

module Fact

  use Int

  let rec function fact (n: int) : int
    requires { n >= 0 }
    variant  { n }
  = if n = 0 then 1 else n * fact (n-1)

end

(** {2 Generic iteration of a function} *)

module Iter

  use Int

  (** `iter k x` is `f^k(x)` *)
  let rec function iter (f: 'a -> 'a) (k: int) (x: 'a) : 'a
    requires { k >= 0 }
    variant  { k }
  = if k = 0 then x else iter f (k - 1) (f x)

  lemma iter_1: forall f, x: 'a. iter f 1 x = f x

  lemma iter_s: forall f, k, x: 'a. 0 < k -> iter f k x = f (iter f (k - 1) x)

end

(** {2 Integers extended with an infinite value} *)

module IntInf

  use Int

  type t = Finite int | Infinite

  let function add (x: t) (y: t) : t =
    match x with
      | Infinite -> Infinite
      | Finite x ->
        match y with
          | Infinite -> Infinite
          | Finite y -> Finite (x + y)
        end
    end

  let predicate eq (x y: t) =
    match x, y with
      | Infinite, Infinite -> true
      | Finite x, Finite y -> x = y
      | _, _ -> false
    end

  let predicate lt (x y: t) =
    match x with
      | Infinite -> false
      | Finite x ->
        match y with
          | Infinite -> true
          | Finite y -> x < y
        end
    end

  let predicate le (x y: t) = lt x y || eq x y

  clone export relations.TotalOrder with type t = t, predicate rel = le,
    lemma Refl, lemma Antisymm, lemma Trans, lemma Total

end

(** {2 Induction principle on integers}

This theory can be cloned with the wanted predicate, to perform an
induction, either on nonnegative integers, or more generally on
integers greater or equal a given bound.

*)

module SimpleInduction

  use Int

  predicate p int

  axiom base: p 0

  axiom induction_step: forall n:int. 0 <= n -> p n -> p (n+1)

  lemma SimpleInduction : forall n:int. 0 <= n -> p n

end

module Induction

  use Int

  predicate p int

  lemma Induction :
    (forall n:int. 0 <= n -> (forall k:int. 0 <= k < n -> p k) -> p n) ->
    forall n:int. 0 <= n -> p n

  constant bound : int

  lemma Induction_bound :
    (forall n:int. bound <= n ->
      (forall k:int. bound <= k < n -> p k) -> p n) ->
    forall n:int. bound <= n -> p n

end

module HOInduction

  use Int

  let lemma induction (p: int -> bool)
    requires { p 0 }
    requires { forall n. 0 <= n >= 0 -> p n -> p (n+1) }
    ensures  { forall n. 0 <= n -> p n }
  = let rec lemma f (n: int) requires { n >= 0 } ensures  { p n } variant {n}
    = if n > 0 then f (n-1) in f 0

end

(** {2 Fibonacci numbers} *)

module Fibonacci

  use Int

  let rec function fib (n: int) : int
    requires { n >= 0 }
    variant  { n }
  = if n = 0 then 0 else
    if n = 1 then 1 else
    fib (n-1) + fib (n-2)

end

module WFltof
  use Int
  use relations.WellFounded

  type t
  function f t : int

  axiom f_nonneg: forall x. 0 <= f x

  predicate ltof (x y: t) = f x < f y

  let rec lemma acc_ltof (n: int)
    requires { 0 <= n }
    ensures  { forall x. f x < n -> acc ltof x }
    variant  { n }
  = if n > 0 then acc_ltof (n-1)

  lemma wf_ltof: well_founded ltof

end

source_heap_reallocation.mlw.text:
(* 2026-10-15 ET. Prospective trusted heap semantics, not an admitted theorem.
   There are no source-specific propositions or recursive equations here.
   Allocation identities are mathematical integers, never machine epochs.
   Imported int.Int arithmetic is a separately inventoried trusted foundation.
*)
module Heap
  use int.Int
  use map.Map

  type cell = Integer int | Pointer int int
  type heap = {
    next : int;
    allocated : map int bool;
    alive : map int bool;
    dynamic : map int bool;
    writable : map int bool;
    extent : map int int;
    address : map int int;
    memory : map int (map int cell);
    initialized : map int (map int bool)
  }

  (* A concrete empty heap used only to prove feasibility of source entries.
     Arbitrary incoming heaps in member obligations remain quantified. *)
  function empty (dummy:int) : heap =
    { next = 1; allocated = (fun _ -> False); alive = (fun _ -> False);
      dynamic = (fun _ -> False); writable = (fun _ -> False);
      extent = (fun _ -> 0); address = (fun _ -> 0);
      memory = (fun _ -> (fun _ -> Integer 0));
      initialized = (fun _ -> (fun _ -> False)) }

  predicate live (h:heap) (b:int) = b <> 0 /\ h.alive[b] = True
  predicate issued (h:heap) (b:int) = h.allocated[b] = True
  predicate separated (h:heap) (b c:int) =
    h.address[b] + h.extent[b] <= h.address[c] \/
    h.address[c] + h.extent[c] <= h.address[b]
  predicate aligned (p alignment:int) = exists q:int. p = alignment*q
  predicate well_formed (h:heap) =
    0 < h.next /\
    (forall b:int. issued h b -> 0 < b < h.next) /\
    (forall b:int. live h b ->
      issued h b /\ 0 <= h.extent[b] /\ 0 < h.address[b]) /\
    (forall b,c:int. live h b /\ live h c /\ b <> c ->
      h.address[b] <> h.address[c] /\ separated h b c)

  (* Allocator output relation from the existing fresh-allocation policy.
     This is a uniform semantic primitive, not a new constructor precondition.
     Incoming receiver/buffer subobjects may overlap within one identity. *)
  predicate available (h:heap) (n a:int) =
    0 <= n /\ 0 < a /\ aligned a 4 /\
    (forall b:int. live h b ->
      a <> h.address[b] /\
      (a + 4*n <= h.address[b] \/ h.address[b] + h.extent[b] <= a))

  function fresh_id (h:heap) : int = h.next
  function bytes (h:heap) (b:int) : int = h.extent[b]
  function numerical_address (h:heap) (b:int) : int = h.address[b]
  predicate same_object (before after:heap) (b:int) =
    before.allocated[b] = after.allocated[b] /\
    before.alive[b] = after.alive[b] /\
    before.dynamic[b] = after.dynamic[b] /\
    before.writable[b] = after.writable[b] /\
    before.extent[b] = after.extent[b] /\
    before.address[b] = after.address[b]
  function contents (h:heap) (b o:int) : cell = h.memory[b][o]
  predicate initialized_at (h:heap) (b o:int) = h.initialized[b][o] = True
  predicate integer_at (h:heap) (b o v:int) = contents h b o = Integer v
  predicate pointer_at (h:heap) (b o target offset:int) =
    contents h b o = Pointer target offset
  predicate forms (h:heap) (b o:int) =
    live h b /\ 0 <= o <= h.extent[b]
  predicate can_read (h:heap) (b o width:int) =
    live h b /\ 0 <= o /\ 0 < width /\ o + width <= h.extent[b]
  predicate can_write (h:heap) (b o width:int) =
    can_read h b o width /\ h.writable[b] = True
  predicate typed_reads (h:heap) (b o width alignment:int) =
    can_read h b o width /\ aligned (h.address[b]+o) alignment
  predicate typed_writes (h:heap) (b o width alignment:int) =
    can_write h b o width /\ aligned (h.address[b]+o) alignment
  predicate typed_forms (h:heap) (b o alignment:int) =
    forms h b o /\ aligned (h.address[b]+o) alignment
  predicate freeable (h:heap) (b o:int) =
    live h b /\ h.dynamic[b] = True /\ o = 0

  (* Uniform allocator primitive. Fresh cells are uninitialized, not filled.
     Address is separate from identity, so reuse never revives an old alias. *)
  function allocate (h:heap) (n a:int) : heap =
    { h with next = h.next + 1;
      allocated = set h.allocated h.next True;
      alive = set h.alive h.next True;
      dynamic = set h.dynamic h.next True;
      writable = set h.writable h.next True;
      extent = set h.extent h.next (4*n);
      address = set h.address h.next a;
      initialized = set h.initialized h.next (fun _ -> False) }

  (* Uniform typed stores. Access checks are separate mapped obligations,
     never pre-proven by these total transition functions. *)
  function put_integer (h:heap) (b o v:int) : heap =
    { h with memory = set h.memory b (set h.memory[b] o (Integer v));
      initialized = set h.initialized b (set h.initialized[b] o True) }
  function put_pointer (h:heap) (b o target offset:int) : heap =
    { h with memory = set h.memory b (set h.memory[b] o (Pointer target offset));
      initialized = set h.initialized b (set h.initialized[b] o True) }

  (* No field reset and no alias rewriting. The null identity is zero. *)
  function release (h:heap) (b:int) : heap =
    if b = 0 then h else { h with alive = set h.alive b False }

  predicate filled_prefix (h:heap) (b k v:int) =
    forall j:int. 0 <= j < k ->
      initialized_at h b (4*j) /\ integer_at h b (4*j) v

  (* 2026-10-16 ET. Source-int embedding, not a new C caller requires.
     Only initialized typed int objects map to Integer cells in range. Pointer
     cells, padding, partial bytes and type-punned objects are not admitted by
     this relation. Every evaluated load has a separate access/type VC. *)
  function load_int (h:heap) (b o:int) : int =
    match contents h b o with
    | Integer v -> v
    | Pointer _ _ -> 0
    end

  predicate int32_at (h:heap) (b o:int) =
    typed_reads h b o 4 4 /\ initialized_at h b o /\
    integer_at h b o (load_int h b o) /\
    -2147483648 <= load_int h b o <= 2147483647
  predicate int32_region (h:heap) (b offset count:int) =
    forall j:int. 0 <= j < count -> int32_at h b (offset+4*j)

  (* Logical image construction from WP Typed's integer chunk, not a C store.
     Machine-range/source-object admission is checked separately. This does
     not assert that old initialized Pointer-tag cells were integer objects. *)
  type int_values = map int int
  function int_chunk_value (values:int_values) (offset:int) : int = values[offset]
  predicate int_slot (offset count p:int) =
    exists j:int. 0 <= j < count /\ p = offset+4*j
  predicate bounded_int_values (values:int_values) (offset count:int) =
    forall j:int. 0 <= j < count ->
      -2147483648 <= values[offset+4*j] <= 2147483647
  function project_int_region (h:heap) (values:int_values) (b offset count:int) : heap =
    { h with memory = set h.memory b
      (fun p -> if int_slot offset count p then Integer values[p] else h.memory[b][p]) }

  (* The entry snapshot contains arbitrary index-specific int values. The
     source stays live/unchanged until release; no uniformly filled input law
     or desired copy theorem is assumed. *)
  function copy_int (h:heap) (source source_offset target target_offset:int) : heap =
    put_integer h target target_offset (load_int h source source_offset)
  predicate copied_prefix (entry now:heap) (source source_offset target count:int) =
    forall j:int. 0 <= j < count ->
      int32_at now target (4*j) /\
      load_int now target (4*j) = load_int entry source (source_offset+4*j)

  (* Source automatic-object placement is a distinct semantic output relation.
     It ranges over arbitrary incoming heaps and unbounded fresh identities;
     no finite pool, epoch limit, dynamic-free permission or empty-heap premise.
     The caller map must bind the actual declaration/cleanup and target layout. *)
  predicate automatic_available (h:heap) (width alignment a:int) =
    0 <= width /\ 0 < a /\ 0 < alignment /\ aligned a alignment /\
    (forall b:int. live h b -> a <> h.address[b] /\
      (a+width <= h.address[b] \/ h.address[b]+h.extent[b] <= a))
  function begin_automatic (h:heap) (width a:int) : heap =
    { h with next = h.next+1;
      allocated = set h.allocated h.next True;
      alive = set h.alive h.next True;
      dynamic = set h.dynamic h.next False;
      writable = set h.writable h.next True;
      extent = set h.extent h.next width;
      address = set h.address h.next a;
      initialized = set h.initialized h.next (fun _ -> False) }
  function end_automatic (h:heap) (b:int) : heap = release h b
end

source_vector_owned_effects.mlw.text:
(* 2026-10-16 ET. Pending header-effect interpretation for original model C.
   No axioms or admitted source propositions. Heap/Owners definitions are
   imported unchanged. Receiver padding is outside this field observation;
   physical padding/frame correspondence remains a separate source duty. *)
module OwnedEffects
  use int.Int
  use map.Map
  use heap_reallocation.Heap as H
  use vector_owned_state.Owners as O

  type phases = map int bool
  predicate is_ready (ready:phases) (r:int) = ready[r] = True
  function target (h:H.heap) (r:int) : int =
    match H.contents h r 0 with
    | H.Pointer b _ -> b
    | H.Integer _ -> 0
    end
  function size (h:H.heap) (r:int) : int = H.load_int h r 8
  function capacity (h:H.heap) (r:int) : int = H.load_int h r 16

  predicate receiver (h:H.heap) (r:int) =
    H.typed_writes h r 0 8 8 /\ H.typed_writes h r 8 8 8 /\
    H.typed_writes h r 16 8 8
  predicate header (h:H.heap) (r b n c:int) =
    receiver h r /\ 0 <= n <= c <= 18446744073709551615 /\
    H.pointer_at h r 0 b 0 /\ H.integer_at h r 8 n /\
    H.integer_at h r 16 c /\ H.initialized_at h r 0 /\
    H.initialized_at h r 8 /\ H.initialized_at h r 16

  (* A reserved destination has no physical field-value premise. Source
     automatic placement/freshness is additional to this phase relation. *)
  predicate reserved (h:H.heap) (s:O.state) (ready:phases) (r:int) =
    O.active_owner s r /\ ready[r] = False /\ O.buffer s r = 0 /\ receiver h r
  predicate world (h:H.heap) (s:O.state) (ready:phases) =
    H.well_formed h /\ O.valid s (H.fresh_id h) /\
    (forall r:int. O.active_owner s r ->
      receiver h r /\
      (ready[r] = True -> exists n,c:int. header h r (O.buffer s r) n c)) /\
    (forall r:int. O.active_owner s r /\ 0 < O.buffer s r ->
      H.freeable h (O.buffer s r) 0)

  function store_header (h:H.heap) (r b n c:int) : H.heap =
    H.put_integer (H.put_integer (H.put_pointer h r 0 b 0) r 8 n) r 16 c
  function copy_header (h:H.heap) (destination source:int) : H.heap =
    store_header h destination (target h source) (size h source) (capacity h source)
  function move (h:H.heap) (destination source:int) : H.heap =
    store_header (copy_header h destination source) source 0 0 0
  function moved_phases (ready:phases) (destination source:int) : phases =
    set (set ready destination True) source True

  (* Exact C temporary order: fresh automatic t = *this; *this = *other;
     *other = t; end t. The temporary is not a second vector owner. *)
  function swap (h:H.heap) (left right a:int) : H.heap =
    let temporary = H.fresh_id h in
    let h1 = H.begin_automatic h 24 a in
    let h2 = copy_header h1 temporary left in
    let h3 = copy_header h2 left right in
    let h4 = copy_header h3 right temporary in
    H.end_automatic h4 temporary

  predicate incoming_frame (before after:H.heap) (left right:int) =
    forall b:int. H.issued before b ->
      H.same_object before after b /\
      (b <> left /\ b <> right -> forall p:int.
        H.contents before b p = H.contents after b p /\
        (H.initialized_at before b p <-> H.initialized_at after b p))
end
